newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian bourse boss renews call for privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian bourse boss renews call for privatisation.

text.p: The president of the Nigerian stock exchange on Tuesday renewed his call on the country's military rulers to privatise state-owned utilities.
Pascal Dozie said at the annual general meeting of the exchange that privatisation would raise efficiency of the affected companies and boost the capital market.
The exchange has consistently called for the privatisation of Nigeria's public utilities to make it worthwhile for foreign investors to come into the market.
Capital market operators said they were disappointed when the government failed to announce a programme for divestment in its 1997 budget.
A visiting World Bank official was quoted in local newspapers on Tuesday as saying the government was determined to resume the privatisation programme.

Dozie said there was still a lot the market could contribute to the long-term development and growth of the economy but added that government had to play its role to boost the market's impact on the national economy.
"Government policies have implications for the growth direction of stock markets," he said.
Dozie said government should also offer fiscal incentives to quoted companies to make quotation attractive to Nigerian businesses.
He suggested the introduction of a discriminatory corporate tax system as obtains in other economies and preferential treatment to quoted companies on government contracts.
Dozie is vacating the position after four years.
He listed as his achievements the opening up of the market to foreign investors, rise in turnover and introduction of an automated clearing and settlement system.
Market capitalisation on the bourse rose to 394 billion naira at the end of April this year from 285.6 billion naira a year ago.
The all-share index rose to 8585.63 on Monday from 6992.10 at the end of 1996, a 22.8 percent increase compared with a 37 percent gain for the whole of 1996.
